name: Shahi Paneer

ingredients.name: Paneer (cottage cheese), full-fat
ingredients.householdMeasure: a fifth of a 500 g block, cut into about 12 cubes of 2 cm

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.householdMeasure: about ¾ cup (100 ml to boil the base, 15 ml for the curd, 60 ml for the gravy)

ingredients.name: Fresh cream (about 25% fat, e.g. a packaged "fresh cream")

equipment: Small saucepan with a lid, to boil the onion-cashew base (any small pot works)
Mixer-grinder with the small chutney jar
Kadai or medium heavy pan with a lid (about 20 cm)
Small bowl and fork or whisk, for the curd
Bowl of warm water, to keep the paneer cubes soft
Measuring spoons and a measuring cup (a normal teaspoon and a steel glass are fine stand-ins)

steps.title: Cube the paneer
steps.text: Cut 100 g paneer into 2 cm cubes (about 12).
steps.visualCue: Even, clean-edged white cubes
steps.cameraCheck: The paneer cubes on the board
steps.videoShot: A knife cutting a paneer block into cubes.

steps.title: Soak the paneer
steps.text: Put the cubes in a bowl of warm (not hot) water and leave them while you cook.
steps.tip: Store-bought paneer can be rubbery; 15–20 minutes in warm water makes it soft again.
steps.visualCue: Cubes fully under water
steps.cameraCheck: The cubes in the water bowl
steps.videoShot: Paneer cubes slipped into warm water.

steps.title: Chop the onion
steps.text: Roughly chop ½ medium onion (60 g).
steps.visualCue: Rough chunks, about ½ cup
steps.videoShot: A knife cutting onion into chunks.

steps.title: Chop the tomato
steps.text: Roughly chop 1 small ripe tomato (80 g).
steps.visualCue: Red chunks, about ⅓ cup
steps.videoShot: Tomato cut into chunks.

steps.title: Prepare ginger, garlic and chilli
steps.text: Slice ½-inch ginger (4 g), peel 2 small garlic cloves (4 g) and slit ½ small green chilli (2 g).
steps.visualCue: Thin ginger slices, two peeled cloves, a slit chilli
steps.videoShot: Ginger being sliced.

steps.title: Load the base pan
steps.text: Put the onion, tomato, 7–8 cashews (10 g), ginger, garlic and chilli into the small saucepan with 100 ml water.
steps.visualCue: Water just covers about half the vegetables
steps.videoShot: Cashews dropped onto onion and tomato in a pan.

steps.title: Boil the base
steps.text: Bring to a boil on medium heat, then cover and simmer on low.
steps.tip: Boiling the onion instead of frying it keeps the gravy pale orange and uses no oil at this stage.
steps.visualCue: Onion translucent and very soft, tomato skin loose, cashews soft enough to press flat
steps.cameraCheck: A cashew pressed with a spoon
steps.videoShot: The lid lifted on a simmering pan.

steps.title: Cool the base
steps.text: Turn off the heat, uncover and let it cool.
steps.tip: Blending a very hot mix can blow the jar lid open.
steps.visualCue: Warm, not steaming hard
steps.videoShot: Steam fading from the pan.

steps.title: Blend the base
steps.text: Tip everything, with its cooking water, into the small mixer jar and blend until completely smooth; add up to 2 tbsp water if it sticks.
steps.tip: Grit means more blending; this step decides how "shahi" (silky) the gravy feels.
steps.visualCue: Silky, pale orange-pink paste with no cashew grit when rubbed between fingers
steps.videoShot: Smooth paste poured from the jar.

steps.title: Whisk the curd
steps.text: Whisk 2 tbsp (30 g) curd with 1 tbsp (15 ml) water until smooth.
steps.visualCue: Smooth, no lumps, like thick buttermilk
steps.videoShot: A fork whisking curd in a bowl.

steps.title: Heat the fat
steps.text: Put the kadai on medium heat with 1 tsp (5 g) ghee and 1 tsp (5 g) oil.
steps.visualCue: Ghee melted, fat shimmering
steps.videoShot: Ghee melting into oil.

steps.title: Temper the whole spices
steps.text: Add 1 bay leaf, 2 cracked cardamom pods, 2 cloves, ½-inch cinnamon and ¼ tsp cumin seeds.
steps.tip: If the cumin turns black at once, the fat is too hot; lower the heat.
steps.visualCue: Cumin sizzles and darkens one shade; cardamom puffs; warm, sweet smell
steps.videoShot: Whole spices crackling in ghee.

steps.title: Add the paste
steps.text: Pour in the blended paste and stir. Stand back; it splutters.
steps.visualCue: Paste spread across the kadai, bubbling
steps.videoShot: Paste poured into the spiced ghee.

steps.title: Cook the paste
steps.text: Cook on medium-low, stirring every 30 seconds.
steps.tip: Half-cover the kadai with the lid if it splashes.
steps.visualCue: Thickens to a mound, turns a shade darker, raw onion smell gone, a little ghee shows at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: The edge of the paste showing ghee
steps.videoShot: Spatula drawing a line through thick paste.

steps.title: Add the powders
steps.text: Lower the heat and add ½ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, ½ tsp coriander powder and a small pinch of turmeric. Stir.
steps.visualCue: Gravy turns a soft orange; spices smell toasted, not burnt
steps.videoShot: Powders sprinkled over the paste and stirred.

steps.title: Add the curd slowly
steps.text: Turn the heat to the lowest. Add the whisked curd 1 tbsp at a time, stirring all the time.
steps.tip: High heat or sour curd makes the gravy split into grains; if it does, blend it smooth again or whisk hard off the heat.
steps.visualCue: Each spoon blends in smoothly before the next; no white specks
steps.cameraCheck: The gravy after the last spoon of curd
steps.videoShot: A spoon of curd stirred into orange gravy.

steps.title: Cook the curd in
steps.text: Keep stirring on low heat.
steps.visualCue: Gravy smooth and glossy again, edges just starting to show fat
steps.videoShot: Close-up of glossy gravy.

steps.title: Season and loosen
steps.text: Add 2 g (⅓ tsp) salt, ¼ tsp (1 g) sugar and 60 ml water. Stir and simmer.
steps.visualCue: Gravy coats the back of a spoon and drips slowly
steps.videoShot: Water poured in, gravy stirred and bubbling gently.

steps.title: Add the paneer
steps.text: Drain the paneer and add the cubes. Fold them in gently and simmer on low.
steps.tip: Fold, don't stir hard; soft paneer breaks easily.
steps.visualCue: Cubes coated in gravy and warmed through
steps.videoShot: Paneer cubes tipped in and folded.

steps.title: Add the cream
steps.text: Pour in 4 tsp (20 ml) fresh cream (and the saffron milk, if using) and fold in.
steps.visualCue: Gravy turns paler and silkier; let it come just to a simmer, not a hard boil
steps.cameraCheck: The swirl of cream in the gravy
steps.videoShot: Cream swirled into the gravy.

steps.title: Finish with garam masala and kasuri methi
steps.text: Sprinkle ¼ tsp garam masala and crush ½ tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the kadai. Stir once and turn off the heat.
steps.visualCue: Green flecks and a warm, sweet smell
steps.cameraCheck: The kasuri methi on the gravy
steps.videoShot: Palms rubbing kasuri methi over the pan.

steps.title: Taste and adjust
steps.text: Taste and add a pinch more salt only if needed; add 1–2 tbsp hot water if it is too thick.
steps.visualCue: Mild, creamy, slightly sweet and nutty, gently spiced
steps.videoShot: A spoon of gravy lifted for tasting.

steps.title: Garnish and serve
steps.text: Remove the bay leaf and cinnamon, transfer to a bowl and scatter 1 tsp chopped coriander leaves on top.
steps.tip: The gravy thickens as it rests; that is normal.
steps.visualCue: Pale-orange, glossy gravy with white paneer cubes and green flecks
steps.videoShot: Coriander scattered over the bowl, steam rising.

reasons: good protein (about 24 g), calcium (about 310 mg) and B12 from paneer, no frying, no maida, and only ¼ tsp sugar. Points off for about 42 g fat with about 21 g saturated fat (close to a full day's limit), about 93 mg cholesterol, about 850 mg sodium, and little fibre or vegetable (about 4 g fibre). Restaurant versions usually use more cream, butter and cashew, sometimes sugar or condensed milk and malai, and come with naan, so 800–1,000 kcal meals are common.

researchRating.basis: a classic, widely loved North Indian restaurant curry; it has its own Wikipedia article, Swiggy's blog lists it among its top-8 must-try paneer dishes, almost every major Indian recipe site publishes it, Hebbar's Kitchen's version shows 4.99 from 184 votes (Hindi page), My Food Story 4.75 from 8, and Veg Recipes of India's page has at least 17 pages of comments; it is sold as a ready meal by MTR. Points off because it is seen as a heavy, special-occasion dish, it is often confused with paneer butter masala and korma, and Mumbai delivery menus list it far less often than paneer butter masala or kadai paneer. Platform dish ratings were not used.

storage: Fridge-safe in a closed box for up to 2 days (cool within 1 hour). Freezer: the gravy alone (without paneer) freezes for up to 1 month; cream-and-curd gravies can turn a little grainy, so whisk well while reheating; frozen paneer turns crumbly, so add fresh paneer when reheating if you can. Reheat in a pan on low with 2–3 tbsp water or milk, stirring gently, until it just bubbles (do not boil hard or the gravy may split); or microwave in 1-minute bursts, stirring between.
leftoverRemix: Shahi paneer kathi roll or toastie. Cook the leftover curry down in a pan until thick and clinging, mash a few paneer cubes, then roll it in a warm roti with sliced onion, a little green chutney and a pinch of chaat masala, and toast the roll on a tawa with ½ tsp oil. Or spread it between two slices of bread with capsicum slices and grill it as a sandwich.
burnOff: about 7.8 km of running (545 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 10.9 km of brisk walking (about 2 h 10 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With 2 phulkas (about 725 kcal): about 10.4 km running or 14.5 km walking (est.).

navratri.reason: paneer, curd, cream, cashews and tomato are allowed in the common vrat rule set; skip onion and garlic, use sendha namak instead of table salt, and leave out turmeric and coriander powder if your family avoids them.

ekadashi.reason: the dish has no grains or pulses; skip onion and garlic (common rule set; family rules on spices vary).

jain.reason: onion, garlic and fresh ginger are root vegetables; use the Jain variant (tomato-cashew gravy, sonth).

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; a filling, high-protein iftar dinner with roti or naan; for sehri it is heavy (about 42 g fat) and fairly salty (about 850 mg sodium), so eat a small bowl and drink water.

jain.reason: onion, garlic and fresh ginger are root vegetables; skip all three, use dry ginger powder (sonth) and a tomato-cashew base (see Jain variant).

vegan.reason: paneer, ghee, curd and cream are dairy; use firm tofu, oil and extra cashews instead (see Vegan variant, Shahi Tofu).

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian, no meat, so it fits a pescatarian diet.

sattvik.reason: skip onion and garlic and build the gravy on tomato, cashew and ginger (see Sattvik variant).

glutenFree.reason: no wheat, maida, rava or besan, and the main recipe uses no hing; if you add hing, use a gluten-free one, as most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour. Check the garam masala label for added flour.

dairyFree.reason: paneer, ghee, curd and cream are dairy; use the Shahi Tofu variant.
